CB30: Investigations

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we look back at some of our most memorable investigative stories over the last three decades.

Summary:
I’ve grouped the stories into six categories – Animal Rights, The Vulnerable (children & the elderly), Medical, Cops, State Enterprises / Government, White Collar Crime/ Companies.


Further information:
The idea is to do quick cuts of different stories for each theme and then expand on one or two of the stories in more detail in that section. I think it’s important to focus on the stories with the best visual moments – obviously there are many great investigatives but some might need a lot of context and explanation and I think it best to keep those to a minimum and showcase golden investigative moments that brought about change.

Script:


THE WILD ONES

VO: Over the years our stories have exposed the ruthless and the corrupt and allowed for the voiceless to be heard and to be defended.

The Wild Ones, are no different – animal rights stories are difficult to tell because of the inhumane degree of mistreatment – the visuals are often horrifying.

We broke the Tuli Elephant Abuse story in 1999 – exposing shocking cruelty to juvenile elephants removed from their natural herds in Botswana. 30 baby elephants were to be trained in the North West and then sold to zoos in Europe and China. The so-called training was nothing more than brutal.

TULI UPSOUND…. The fact that it was wrong.

VO: Carte Blanche has exposed illegal bush racing rings, unscrupulous pet shops, animal cruelty in the chicken farming industry – where we uncovered how new born chicks were killed within hours of emerging from the shell.

We’ve investigated the illegal trade of rhino horn and more recently, lion bones.

BONE CHILLING UPSOUND: …. a wine that has no medicinal value.

VO: Carte Blanche has traveled the world to expose extreme animal rights violations. In 2015 – the spotlight was on the Faroe Islands where we brought you scenes of the disturbing mass slaughter of pilot whales.

FAROE ISLAND UPSOUND….. thing I have ever seen in my life.

HEALTH HORRORS

VO: The public and private health sectors have served up a fair share of rogues over the last three decades. From crumbling public health departments to illegally selling prescription drugs to botched plastic surgeries and DIY abortions.

While abortion is legal in South Africa, accessing the service is not always so straight forward. In 2002 we went undercover to investigate abortions at state clinics. Our finding were shocking….

HIDDEN CAMERA FOOTAGE: …. Pull it out and throw it away.

VO: We’ve exposed the chronic failures in the Health Department from severe staff shortages to decaying infrastructure and overcrowded hospitals across the country.

The LIFE Esidemeni tragedy saw the death of 156 mentally-ill patients under the care of unlicensed NGOs appointed by the state. We put Gauteng Health MEC Qedani Mahlangu in the hotseat for the first time.

LIFE ESIDEMENI UPSOUND….. I know my constitutional responsibility and that of my department.

VO: While the MEC claimed ignorance. The Esidemeni Arbitration hearings did not accepted that excuse.

JUSTICE DIKGANG MOSENEKE UPSOUND: Miss Mahlangu was responsible. She was the ultimate leader and commander of the project.

CROOKED COPS

VO: The police are there to protect and serve. But in the South African context the police have often left much to be desired.

We’ve exposed police brutality with cops physically assaulting civilians.

And caught them on camera time and time again abusing their power… taking bribes for traffic violations in 1997…. and then again in 2008.

TRAFFIC BRIBES UPSOUND…. R130….

VO: Corrupt cops have been exposed even using police vehicles to commit crimes from hijacking petrol tankers to transporting stolen goods.

THIEVING COPS UPSOUND: ….keeps watch on the road.

VO: In 2004 Carte Blanche showed the ease with which a police docket could potentially disappear. We showed the alarming lack of vigilance when it came to guarding the contents of police files.

Watch as our operative casually accesses dockets without ever impersonating a police officer.

VISH UPSOUND: …like I’ve experienced now.

STATE CORRUPTION

VO: If there’s one thing we’ve learnt, it’s that dodgy people will take any opportunity to make some extra cash.

Be it dipping into letters and parcels at the post office or by helping themselves to items in airline passengers luggage.

UPSOUND: Bingo... for her Kruger safari.

VO: Carte Blanche exposed drivers licence fraud in 1999, 2002 and twice in 2013.

And even showed how road traffic regulations are ignored - endangering South Africans….

We revealed how easy it was to get a wreck of a truck roadworthied - literally giving the green light to weapons on wheels.

WEAPONS ON WHEELS DEREK UPSOUND: … you counting the money.

VO: But sometimes the looting is next level - with corrupt officials crippling municipalities while infrastructure and services fail communities.

We exposed dodgy tenders at City Power in Johannesburg involving a R640 million contract for locally manufactured solar geysers. The culprits were supplying geysers that were non-compliant.

CHINESE GEYSERS UPSOUND Bongani: … stainless steel is not locally produced.

VO: Deep seated corruption and mismanagement at state owned enterprises have kept us busy… with a number of exposes on SAA, and the biggest repeat offender Eskom...

In 2016, our investigation into the pre-payment made by Eskom to the Gupta owned Tegeta revealed just how deep the corruption went at the state power utility.

Mashelo Koko was caught out on camera and admitted he made a mistake.

Carte Blanche’s discoveries formed part of the Public Protector’s State of Capture Report.


WHITE COLLAR CRIME // COMPANIES

VO: Shameless thieving is not restricted to the government…. white collar criminals have been making big bucks off the backs of hard working South Africans with their schemes.

From fake olive oil traders duping bargain hunting consumers to exposing a syndicate buying up black market gold in an ingenious scam netting billions.

Carte Blanche In 2012 exposed an unholy alliance that raked in millions of rands…

UNHOLY ALLIANCE UPSOUND: blown the lid off these secret dealings.

VO: The ring leaders behind Auction Alliance ducked and dived - but we tracked them down.

UPSOUND UNHOLY ALLIANCE 2
Devi: 'Hi Rael, how are you?' [On intercom]
Man 2: 'Fine thank you.'
Devi: 'It's Devi, Carte Blanche.' [On intercom]
Man 2: 'From where?'
Devi: 'Is that Rael Levitt?' [On intercom]
Man 2: 'Yes.'
Devi: 'It's Devi from Carte Blanche.' [On intercom]
Man: Let me check if he’s gone out…

VO: Suddenly the voice changed….

Devi: 'Hi!'
Man 2: 'He's just gone out now, madam.'
Devi: "Are you sure because you said he was here?' [On intercom]
Man 2: 'No , he's not here.'

VO: In 2016 we exposed personal injury lawyer Ronald Bobroff’s looting from his clients. He claimed contingency commissions of upto 25% of clients payout…. In legal terms it’s called over reaching - an illegal practice.

BOBROFF UPSOUND…. We can agree to disagree…

THE VULNERABLE – CHILDREN & THE ELDERLY

VO: But Some of the most unsettling stories we’ve covered lifted the lid on horrendous abuse cases - where the targets have been the elderly and children - the most vulnerable of society who often can not speak for themselves…

HIDDEN CAMERA UPSOUND – hitting the old lady… fight back…

VO: In 2001, we captured appalling physical and psychological elder abuse at an old age home in KwaZulu Natal.

The nursing staff didn't know they were being filmed on hidden camera.

ELDER ABUSE 2001 UPSOUND HIDDEN CAMERA: … die… laughs….

VO: Then 14 years later, horrific footage revealed the ongoing, brutal assaults of an 84-year-old woman entrusted to the care of an East London facility for the aged.

Here you can see the nurse abusing Hope Shepperd.

ELDER ABUSE 2015 UPSOUND: …. Hits her with a deodrant spray can.

VO: Ncendiswa Mkencele was as sentenced to 15 years imprisonment on five counts of assault - the magistrate ordered that she serve at least 8 years.

CUT In yet another explosive expose we revealed the truth behind an unregistered place of safety for abused and neglected children. Under-aged sex, verbal and physical abuse were the order of the day at Jedidiah Safe Haven in Hartbeespoort, run by Stephanie Bentley.

SAFE HAVEN UPSOUND Derek: We’ve actually got video evidence….. EINA! Crying….

VO: Stephanie Bentley eventually admitted guilt, she was criminally charged - but the Director of Public Prosecutions declined to prosecute. All the children under her care were removed and re-homed.

Over the last thirty years we have given you the right to see it all – and we will continue to expose the injustice plaguing our society - because truth brings change.


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Over the last three decades our stories have exposed the ruthless and the corrupt and have allowed for the voiceless to be heard and to be defended - we revisit some of Carte Blanche’s most explosive investigative stories.

PROMO 2

VO: We look back at some of our most memorable investigative stories over the last three decades from animal rights violations to corrupt cops, from health horrors to shocking abuse cases.

UPSOUND….
